html:
The Torrijos-Carter Treaties were signed in Washington on 7 September 1977 by Panama's leader Omar Torrijos and President Jimmy Carter. They provided for Panama to take full control of the Panama Canal by the end of 1999.

The 1903 treaty that followed the separation from Colombia had given the United States a zone across Panama forever. Panamanians resented it, and riots in 1964 left over twenty dead. Torrijos made the canal a world cause.

The treaties were narrowly ratified by the US Senate in 1978. One treaty lets the United States defend the canal's neutrality. The zone was dissolved, and at noon on 31 December 1999 Panama took over the canal, which it has run since, including its expansion in 2016. It was one of the largest handovers of territory of the late Cold War era.
